contract.objective: Make AC-v2 the only current material intent source for new campaigns.
contract.background: Intent closure begins with immutable acceptance. Silent edits or legacy acceptance carry-forward would invalidate the whole protocol.
contract.implementation_approach: Represent sealed AC by fingerprint and sequence. All downstream artifacts store the AC fingerprint they bind. Rebase is a new sequence, not an in-place edit.
success_criteria: `acceptance set|validate|seal|status|rebase` exist and enforce AC-v2 required fields.
Seal requires intent-open state, no open review batch, valid schema, and current authority.
Rebase requires reason, authority, new sequence, new fingerprint, archive of old AC, downstream invalidation, and `acceptance-rebased` event.
`migrate intent-closed` archives state v2/MRPC artifacts, creates state v3, accepts no legacy AC/CEB/kernel as current truth, and blocks mutation until new gates pass.
risks: Migration may accidentally mark legacy artifacts accepted; tests must assert all current acceptance/kernel flags are false after migration.
Rebase invalidation can miss proof or closure artifacts if invalidation is not centralized.

items.step: Implement review batches, RAP-v1 apertures, receipts, and mutation guard v2
acceptance: `review batch begin|status|seal|invalidate`, `review aperture add`, `review receipt add`, and `review plan|status` exist.
Only one review batch can be open; begin validates sealed AC, artifact head, and mode-specific phase permissions.
Conformance RAP-v1 apertures reject whole-diff scope and require law/owner/operation/transition/proof target, excluded scope, and existing class refs.
Batch seal requires complete apertures, terminal receipts, classified claims, valid CEX for confirmed claims, no unknown intent relation, zero mutation events, and unchanged artifact head.
Guard v2 returns machine-readable `resolve_guard_denial` and persists denied mutation attempts.

contract.objective: Make review discovery, conformance, kernel review, and terminal holdout explicit sealed batches with mutation barriers.
contract.background: The protocol forbids mutation while review is open and forbids generic post-kernel conformance. Review lifecycle must be mechanically enforced before CEX/basis work can be trusted.
contract.implementation_approach: Store batch, aperture, and receipt artifacts under `.ledger/c3/review`. Enforce head and mode gates at begin/seal. Wire guard checks to state and open batch ids.
success_criteria: `review batch begin|status|seal|invalidate`, `review aperture add`, `review receipt add`, and `review plan|status` exist.
Only one review batch can be open; begin validates sealed AC, artifact head, and mode-specific phase permissions.
Conformance RAP-v1 apertures reject whole-diff scope and require law/owner/operation/transition/proof target, excluded scope, and existing class refs.
Batch seal requires complete apertures, terminal receipts, classified claims, valid CEX for confirmed claims, no unknown intent relation, zero mutation events, and unchanged artifact head.
Guard v2 returns machine-readable `resolve_guard_denial` and persists denied mutation attempts.
risks: Treating outdated unresolved review threads as harmless can bypass mutation barriers; seal must classify all claims.
Whole-diff conformance may sneak in through missing aperture fields; conformance validation must be mode-specific.

items.step: Implement CEX-v1 admission, classification, and CEB-v2 sealing
acceptance: `counterexample add|classify|list|show` and `basis compile|lint|seal|status` exist.
CEX-v1 schema validates intent relation, novelty, disposition, AC anchors, minimal trace for confirmed in-horizon CEX, and aperture ref for conformance CEX.
Caller-provided mutation authority is rejected or ignored; controller-derived mutation authority is always false at finding level.
Provisional classifications have no mutation or invalidation authority until CEB-v2 seal.
CEB-v2 includes every accepted in-horizon CEX exactly once, quotients duplicates, rejects unknown novelty, and records law/acceptance refs, canonical owner, proof obligation, and congruence evidence.

contract.objective: Separate raw/provisional review evidence from sealed counterexample classes and basis authority.
contract.background: The central CEGIS invariant is that findings become evidence, not patches. The sealed basis is the first point where recurrence and novelty can control downstream invalidation.
contract.implementation_approach: Append CEX records, update classifications deterministically, and compile a sealed basis only from sealed review batches. Gate all same-class and novel-class transitions on sealed CEB fingerprint.
success_criteria: `counterexample add|classify|list|show` and `basis compile|lint|seal|status` exist.
CEX-v1 schema validates intent relation, novelty, disposition, AC anchors, minimal trace for confirmed in-horizon CEX, and aperture ref for conformance CEX.
Caller-provided mutation authority is rejected or ignored; controller-derived mutation authority is always false at finding level.
Provisional classifications have no mutation or invalidation authority until CEB-v2 seal.
CEB-v2 includes every accepted in-horizon CEX exactly once, quotients duplicates, rejects unknown novelty, and records law/acceptance refs, canonical owner, proof obligation, and congruence evidence.
risks: Provisional labels can accidentally control realization invalidation; add a direct negative regression.
Duplicate quotienting can hide a distinct class if congruence evidence is missing; fail closed on unresolved congruence.

items.step: Bind MBK, reduction, and design acceptance to AC/CEB fingerprints
acceptance: Kernel, reduction, and design acceptance require current sealed AC and CEB fingerprints.
`reduction_certificate_v1` is advertised and either has `reduction set|lint|review|accept` commands or an equivalent explicit reduction path.
Unanchored observations, laws with no AC refs, outside-horizon classes, MAY-only laws, unwitnessed distinctions, unresolved congruence, non-goal leakage, and missing recomposition are rejected.
Kernel acceptance records AC, CEB, MBK, and RC fingerprints.

contract.objective: Prevent kernel growth and design distinctions that lack accepted counterexample witnesses.
contract.background: MBK/RC/design surfaces already exist in 0.2.x, but they are not intent-closed unless every retained distinction maps to sealed AC and CEB authority.
contract.implementation_approach: Extend validators to require fingerprint bindings and law/class mappings. Preserve existing command compatibility while strengthening gates.
success_criteria: Kernel, reduction, and design acceptance require current sealed AC and CEB fingerprints.
`reduction_certificate_v1` is advertised and either has `reduction set|lint|review|accept` commands or an equivalent explicit reduction path.
Unanchored observations, laws with no AC refs, outside-horizon classes, MAY-only laws, unwitnessed distinctions, unresolved congruence, non-goal leakage, and missing recomposition are rejected.
Kernel acceptance records AC, CEB, MBK, and RC fingerprints.
risks: Backward-compatible command aliases may bypass new gates; route every alias through the same validator.
Over-accepting MAY-only laws would grow the semantic surface without proof.

items.step: Implement realization, targeted conformance, PHI-v1, and proof compression gates
acceptance: Realization cycle starts only from accepted kernel/design and campaign base.
Conformance batch is required after realization capture and must use targeted apertures.

Same-class recurrence invalidates design/realization/proof/potential while preserving kernel; novel in-horizon class invalidates basis/kernel/design/realization; contract-invalidating CEX returns to intent-open.

`potential baseline|measure|gate|status` recomputes PHI-v1 from raw metric evidence and rejects equal primary tuple, hard-surface growth, proof-debt growth, stale AC cycle, and caller-supplied booleans.
Proof compression maps actions to AC law refs, CEB class refs, recomposition obligations, artifact fingerprint, and invalidators; proof-mutated tree is rejected.

contract.objective: Make one realization cycle prove targeted conformance and strict semantic progress before delivery.
contract.background: Post-kernel work is conformance and semantic progress proof, not a place for broad review or local patch accumulation.
contract.implementation_approach: Bind realization/proof/potential artifacts to accepted fingerprints. Compute PHI from stored metric evidence. Reject stale or broad proof basis.
success_criteria: Realization cycle starts only from accepted kernel/design and campaign base.
Conformance batch is required after realization capture and must use targeted apertures.

Same-class recurrence invalidates design/realization/proof/potential while preserving kernel; novel in-horizon class invalidates basis/kernel/design/realization; contract-invalidating CEX returns to intent-open.

`potential baseline|measure|gate|status` recomputes PHI-v1 from raw metric evidence and rejects equal primary tuple, hard-surface growth, proof-debt growth, stale AC cycle, and caller-supplied booleans.
Proof compression maps actions to AC law refs, CEB class refs, recomposition obligations, artifact fingerprint, and invalidators; proof-mutated tree is rejected.
risks: PHI implementation can become a line-count proxy; tests must verify semantic tuple and hard dimensions.
Proof commands can mutate tree; retain existing tree-stability guard and strengthen stale tree checks.

items.step: Gate physical delivery, tuple closure, terminal holdout, and terminal closure
acceptance: `delivery apply|commit|push` require no open batch, current AC/CEB/MBK/RC/design/realization, sealed clean conformance, PHI strict progress, valid semantic surface, and current proof basis.
Apply creates a backup ref and replaces the delivery tree from the captured realization tree.
Commit and push bind exact delivery tree/head.
Tuple closure requires current targeted conformance and PR sweep evidence.

Terminal closure additionally requires one sealed clean terminal holdout, zero novel in-horizon CEX, zero unknown CEX, zero unresolved contract-invalidating CEX, terminal PHI, current proof/delivery tuple, and reopen conditions.

contract.objective: Preserve physical apply/commit/push ownership while tightening closure to current tuple and terminal evidence.
contract.background: Physical delivery is currently controller-owned and must remain so. The new protocol adds conformance, PHI, and terminal holdout gates before closure.
contract.implementation_approach: Extend existing delivery and certify commands with current fingerprint checks and terminal holdout state. Keep exact-tree backup and match-head semantics.
success_criteria: `delivery apply|commit|push` require no open batch, current AC/CEB/MBK/RC/design/realization, sealed clean conformance, PHI strict progress, valid semantic surface, and current proof basis.
Apply creates a backup ref and replaces the delivery tree from the captured realization tree.
Commit and push bind exact delivery tree/head.
Tuple closure requires current targeted conformance and PR sweep evidence.

Terminal closure additionally requires one sealed clean terminal holdout, zero novel in-horizon CEX, zero unknown CEX, zero unresolved contract-invalidating CEX, terminal PHI, current proof/delivery tuple, and reopen conditions.
risks: Local commit/push could bypass controller; guard and docs must keep raw delivery operations denied in active campaigns.
Terminal closure can be falsely inferred from prose; only controller state and receipts count.

items.step: Ship PR, sweep review, monitor checks, guarded squash-merge, and cleanup
acceptance: A scoped PR is opened or updated from `feature/resolve-c3-intent-closed-cegis`.
PR body includes implementation summary, proof commands, release/tap posture, and caveats.
Required checks are green.
Complete paginated review-thread sweep immediately before merge shows zero unresolved threads on the exact `headRefOid`.

Merge uses `gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch --match-head-commit FRESH_HEAD_REF_OID`, where `FRESH_HEAD_REF_OID` is the PR `headRefOid` fetched after the final push, final checks, and final review-thread sweep.
Local main is updated and feature branch cleanup is complete.

contract.objective: Land the implementation only after the graph, proof, release posture, checks, and review threads are current and clean.
contract.background: The active objective includes `$land`, so closure is not complete at PR creation. Landing requires current-head checks, review-thread inventory, guarded merge, and cleanup.
contract.implementation_approach: Follow `$land`: identify PR, push final branch, watch checks, fetch full review thread inventory with pagination, resolve addressed threads, rerun final sweep matching fresh `headRefOid`, squash-merge with match-head guard, fetch main, switch to main, and delete local branch if present.
success_criteria: A scoped PR is opened or updated from `feature/resolve-c3-intent-closed-cegis`.
PR body includes implementation summary, proof commands, release/tap posture, and caveats.
Required checks are green.

Local main is updated and feature branch cleanup is complete.
risks: Any push after thread/check proof invalidates the closeout sweep.
Review or CI can produce new implementation work; return to the appropriate graph frontier instead of forcing merge.

intent.text: Material graph aperture compilation must use one shared graph analysis and emit current GCR-v1/ST-R1 evidence.
Invalid hard-dependency graphs must block analytics and selection before any critical-depth, reachability, or wave planning runs.
Safe parallel waves must be selected using lock-root/resource conflicts, not selected first and labeled unsafe later.
Intake diagnostics, graph debt, proof basis, and multi-proof receipts must become first-class control surfaces.
v3 files, graph-envelope-v1 reads, simple task mode, and plan_sync v3 consumers must remain compatible.
Dotfiles st skill, agent metadata, and hooks must route material work through GCR after CLI behavior is stable.
Completion requires local Zig proof, compatibility fixtures, skill/hook validation, and PR landing checks.
`seq review-compiler-audit` must support `--protocol auto|legacy-cleanroom|c3`, defaulting to `auto`, without creating a second command.
True C3 detection must require assistant/tool evidence for review_compile.py begin, .resolve-c3/state.json, minimal_review_patch_certificate, or MRPC-v1; raw `$resolve` text is candidate-only.
Historical cleanroom counters must remain available under legacy_cleanroom and must not be combined with CEB/MRPC counters.
C3 audit output must expose denominator, controller, counterexamples, tournament, semantic_cost, ablation, lab_vs_delivery, holdout, delivery, and compliance sections in markdown and JSON.
Event ordering must use .resolve-c3/events.jsonl transcript evidence when present and otherwise derive ordered evidence from assistant text and controller tool records.
Delivery mutation violations must be counted only between begin and closed or aborted, excluding lab/candidate worktree activity and compliant controller commit/push/apply events.
The twelve user-specified C3/legacy scenarios must be covered by focused Zig fixture tests and local seq proof commands.
README, help text, and apps/seq/VERSION must reflect the shipped protocol option.
Implement resolve-c3 state v2, canonical artifacts, RC3-R1 receipts, append-only events, and MBKC-v1 foundations.
Campaign base and review-ready baseline are immutable; rebaseline archives old campaign and creates a new campaign.
Observations refine one accepted Minimum Behavioral Kernel before realization or delivery mutation.
Realization capture and semantic measurement are controller-derived and whole-PR relative to campaign_base_sha.
Proof is planned, executed, compressed, tree-bound, and rejects tree mutation.
Delivery apply, commit, and push are physical Git operations with backup refs, tree checks, and lease checks.
Tuple closure and terminal closure are distinct, fingerprint-bound, and stop-guarded.
MRPC/v1 migration archives safely and never fabricates accepted kernel state.
Existing guard-hook, hook-context, stop-guard integrations remain fail-closed and informative.
seq can reconstruct MBKC-v1 campaigns from state, events, artifacts, and certificate evidence.
`seq review-compiler-audit` must add `--protocol mbk` and `--protocol c3-mrpc` while preserving existing `auto|legacy-cleanroom|c3` behavior.
MBK counters may increment only after MBKC context evidence such as `MBKC-v1`, `minimum_behavioral_kernel`, `resolve-c3 campaign begin`, `kernel-accepted`, or `terminal-closed`.
MBK output must include denominator, campaigns, observations, kernel, realization, semantic_surface, proof, controller, closure, key_metrics, evidence_ledger, and legacy_cleanroom sections.
Physical controller actions, state-only actions, raw apply/commit/push bypasses, tuple closure, and terminal closure must be separately recognized.
Semantic metrics must remain separate from base-relative Git tree metrics and MRPC counts must not mix with MBKC counts.
The ten requested MBK scenarios must be covered by fixture-backed Zig tests while historical MRPC fixtures remain stable.
README/help must document `mbk`, `c3-mrpc`, raw mention exclusion, protocol separation, and MBK example usage.
Add `seq skill-decision-audit` as a deterministic decision-provenance surface that emits STE-v1 and never turns co-occurrence into causality.
Add SKDC-v1 and SDR-v1 parsing, validation, canonical fingerprinting, and companion validation/scaffold commands.
Expose normalized datasets for contract clauses, receipts, decision signals, decision episodes, and decision outcomes through generic `seq query`.
Share skill activation classification with existing `skill-evidence` and `skill-audit` behavior so raw mentions and injected blocks do not inflate activation.
Compile conservative decision episodes, trigger misses/false activations, clause compliance, outcome associations, worker proof edges, gap signatures, and workaround signals.
Add SDD-v1 delta/cursor mode for one-session `$shadow` usage with cursor invalidation on file identity, truncation, or contract fingerprint changes.
Render summary, episodes, misses, clauses, outcomes, tune-packet, delta, and markdown reports with privacy-safe defaults and SEQ-R1 receipts.
Extend `seq capabilities --format json` to advertise skill decision audit, delta, contract, receipt, tune packet, and matched cohort capability states.
Add fixture-heavy tests, including a causality firewall proving weak associations and successful outcomes cannot enter explicit-effect counts.
Update `apps/seq/README.md` and `apps/seq/VERSION` for the release-relevant CLI surface.
Add `seq decision-capsule` as a deterministic DCP-v1 producer for one visible historical decision.
Bind every DCP claim to visible session evidence and exact one-based turn anchors; do not infer private rationale or use today's checkout for historical state.
Compile deterministic decision candidates from SDR/skill episodes, structured route fields, and explicit visible prose while failing closed on ambiguity and contamination.
Expose capsule, candidates, anchors, and validate modes with JSON, JSONL, CSV, table, and Markdown-compatible output where specified.
Add generic query datasets `historical_decisions` and `decision_capsules` plus capability flags for decision capsule support.

Prove source resolution, candidate selection, evidence extraction, outcome boundaries, anchor arithmetic, artifact state honesty, contamination/privacy, schema/output, query datasets, and release gates.
CAS session inquiry must accept rollout-backed DCPs with null `source.thread_id` when `source.rollout_path` exists and RIP workspace policy is `transcript_only`.
CAS must not depend on seq application command/query/dataset surfaces; seq and cas share only a narrow retrace core library.
CAS must verify source and anchor digests with the same canonical algorithm used by seq before starting transcript replay turns.
Rollout transcript replay receipts must truthfully distinguish transcript lineage from app-server `thread/fork` lineage.
Existing thread-backed DCP behavior must remain unchanged.
Validation must include seq tests, CAS session-inquiry tests, aggregate CAS tests, ReleaseFast CAS build, and a regression proving the prior DCP no longer fails at `source_not_found`.
Add a read-only `seq actuation-audit` command that produces deterministic actuation run ledgers from canonical session/tool/worker traces and explicit protocol artifacts.
Preserve evidence authority by accepting GCR/AFR/ARH/FPSR/ASR/SDR only from structured command output, persisted artifacts, or canonical receipt blocks, never from prose.
Expose actuation run, slice, graph-event, proof, compaction, and worker datasets through generic `seq query`.
Implement strict mode with exit code 2 for defined graph-control, frontier, proof, ship, and land violations.
Update capabilities, README, release command-surface gate, fixtures, tests, and `apps/seq/VERSION` for seq 0.3.9.
Prove the feature with focused fixtures, dataset queries, `zig build test`, and the seq release command-surface gate.
Ship and land the validated PR using ready-PR proof, complete review-thread sweep, green checks, and guarded squash merge.
Post-merge PR #35 review findings against `seq actuation-audit` must be validated and repaired at the owning code boundaries.
Audit command selectors and accepted flags must produce bounded, observable behavior instead of silently scanning the wrong corpus or ignoring inputs.
Actuation audit evidence classifiers must not treat command output, failed patches, or failed proof commands as successful control/proof evidence.
Rendered diagnostic and decisions outputs must expose valid, advertised queryable fields.
Release app selection must not carry stale app context across unrelated `build.zig` hunks.
Focused fixtures plus aggregate Zig and release checks must prove the remediation before shipping and landing a follow-up PR.

`resolve-c3` must write `resolve-c3-state-v3` with canonical JSON, stable fingerprints, ordered events, bounded reads, locks, and atomic artifact writes before any new protocol command depends on state.
AC-v2 must be set, validated, sealed, statused, and explicitly rebased; sealed AC must never be edited in place and rebase must archive and invalidate downstream artifacts.
Review batches, RAP-v1 apertures, receipts, and mutation guard v2 must enforce one open batch, mode permissions, conformance targeting, and fail-closed mutation barriers.
CEX-v1 and CEB-v2 must separate provisional evidence from mutation authority, seal only intent-anchored quotientable classes, and reject unresolved novelty.
MBK/RC/design acceptance must bind current AC and CEB fingerprints and reject unanchored or unwitnessed distinctions, MAY-only laws, non-goal leakage, and missing recomposition.

Realization, targeted conformance, PHI-v1, proof compression, delivery, tuple closure, and terminal closure must fail closed on stale artifacts, broad conformance, surface growth, proof debt, or missing clean holdout.
The implementation must add scenario coverage for the supplied 114 tests plus provisional-label non-authority, protocol fixture replay, command smokes, storage/security checks, and release/tap proof.
Shipped closure requires `apps/resolve-c3/VERSION=0.3.0`, repository release assets, Homebrew tap update, `brew audit/test`, and installed binary version/capability proof.
